reasons: The loading overlay shows fixed status text, which can mislead the user about progress.
The Button and Info imports appear unused in the code shown.

terms.meaning: A clickable label that switches the main screen to a different view.
A layer drawn over the whole screen to block clicks and show a message.
Remembered information that can change over time, such as which tab is open.
An animation library used here for the fade and slide effects.
One saved working set of inputs and results on the backend, identified by an ID.

sections.name: File setup, ViewMode
sections.title: Imports and view names
sections.what: Brings in the libraries, the store, the five panel screens, the Button component, and icons, then defines the five allowed view names.
sections.why: Fixing the list of view names means a mistyped view name cannot open a view that does not exist.
sections.watch_out: Adding a tab requires changing this list together with the tab and display code.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 1)
sections.title: Starting tab and header
sections.what: Sets the starting tab to the input view and draws the header with the app title, subtitle, and a session badge showing the first eight characters of the session ID once one exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: a short session ID gives the user a reference without showing a long string.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 2)
sections.title: Tab buttons and instructions
sections.what: Draws the five tab buttons. Results and diagram need outputs, lecture needs a lecture sequence, and research needs at least one research item, otherwise the tab is greyed out. Also draws a three-step instruction strip.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocking empty views and guiding the user through the order of work.
sections.watch_out: Greying out a tab does not change which tab is open, so the screen depends on the content checks in the next section.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 3)
sections.title: Loading overlay during analysis
sections.what: While a calculation runs, shows a full-screen dimmed overlay with a spinning sun, four agent cards, and a note that the wait usually takes 30 to 60 seconds. The cards are fixed text, not live progress.
sections.why: Likely reason: a clear working message stops the user clicking again during a slow run.
sections.watch_out: The 30 to 60 second estimate is written into the text, so the message will be wrong if real runs take longer.

sections.name: Dashboard (part 4)
sections.title: Panel display and footer
sections.what: Shows the panel matching the open tab with a short fade and slide, but only when that panel's data exists. Draws a footer that lists the four agents.
sections.why: Likely reason: checking for data here stops a panel from opening before its data is ready.
sections.watch_out: The footer's agent count is fixed text and will not update if the number of agents changes.

sections.name: AgentStatusProps
sections.title: Agent card settings shape
sections.what: Describes what each agent card needs: a name, a description, a status (active, complete, or pending), and an icon.
sections.why: Gives every card the same shape so they look alike.
sections.watch_out: Only the active status is drawn with a Running label; complete and pending show nothing on the right.

sections.name: AgentStatus
sections.title: Agent status card
sections.what: Draws one agent card with its icon, name, and description, and a pulsing green dot with the word Running when the agent is active.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each agent a visible status line in the loading overlay.
sections.watch_out: Adding a complete or pending look needs new drawing code, because those states currently show nothing.

sections.name: TabButtonProps
sections.title: Tab settings shape
sections.what: Describes one tab: its icon, label, whether it is open, the click action, and whether it is greyed out.
sections.why: Keeps every tab built the same way.

sections.name: TabButton
sections.title: Tab button drawing
sections.what: Draws one tab. An open tab has a white background and a red underline. A disabled tab is faded and cannot be clicked.
sections.why: Likely reason: the visual change shows which view is open and which are not ready.
sections.watch_out: The faded look is only styling; the disabled setting is what blocks clicks, so both must be kept.

summary: The main screen frame: a header with the title and session badge, five tabs for switching views, a full-screen overlay shown while analysis runs, and a footer.
purpose: Lets the user move between the input, results, diagram, lecture, and research views, and tells the user when analysis is running.
why: Likely reason: tabs that are greyed out until their data exists stop the user opening empty views.
how: Keeps the currently open tab in local memory. Reads outputs, the lecture sequence, the research list, the calculating flag, and the session ID from the store. Draws the header, the tabs, a short three-step instruction strip, the loading overlay during a run, the chosen panel with a fade animation, and the footer.
inputs: Store values: outputs, lectureSequence, webResearch, calculating, and sessionId. The user's tab clicks.
outputs: The visible screen, the open panel, and the loading overlay during a calculation.
risks: The four agent cards in the overlay are fixed text that always says Running, so they do not show real progress. The footer's agent count is also fixed text.
debug: If a tab stays greyed out, check that the matching store value (outputs, lectureSequence, or webResearch) is filled after a run. If the overlay never closes, check that calculating is reset to false when a run ends, including when it fails.
